birds.name: Wild Turkey
birds.call: The male’s gobble: a rapid, descending rattle that carries a mile. Hens yelp, cluck and purr.
birds.fact: Wild turkeys can run about 25 mph and burst into flight at up to 55 mph.
birds.nursery: Gobbles most at dawn, mealtimes, and the exact moment you sit down. Puffs up when wearing a fresh onesie.

birds.name: American Crow
birds.call: Harsh, nasal “caw-caw-caw”, usually in a series.
birds.fact: Crows recognise individual human faces and remember people who wronged them for years.
birds.nursery: Recognises whoever does night feeds. Holds grudges about bath time.

birds.name: Common Raven
birds.call: Deep, croaking “prruk”, plus gurgles, knocks and bell-like notes.
birds.fact: Ravens play: they have been filmed sliding down snowy roofs, apparently for fun.
birds.nursery: Prefers low gurgling croaks. Known to steal shiny objects such as keys and phones.

birds.name: Mourning Dove
birds.call: A soft, mournful “coo-OO-oo, oo, oo”.
birds.fact: The whistle you hear when they take off is made by their wing feathers, not their voice.
birds.nursery: Peak cooing occurs mid-morning, usually right after a successful burp.

birds.name: Great Horned Owl
birds.call: Deep, soft hoots: “hoo-h’HOO, hoo, hoo”.
birds.fact: Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees.
birds.nursery: Strictly nocturnal, especially 2–4 a.m. Head rotation limited but enthusiastic.

birds.name: Barred Owl
birds.call: “Who cooks for you? Who cooks for you-all?” plus wild cackling duets.
birds.fact: Mated pairs duet in an eruption of hoots and caterwauls.
birds.nursery: Asks “who cooks for you?” roughly every three hours. The answer is you.

birds.name: Common Loon
birds.call: Haunting wails, yodels and a quavering tremolo “laugh”.
birds.fact: A loon’s legs sit so far back that it can barely walk on land.
birds.nursery: Tremolo laugh triggered by peekaboo. Also cannot walk on land yet.

birds.name: Laughing Kookaburra
birds.call: A rollicking “koo-koo-koo-kaa-kaa-kaa” laughing chorus.
birds.fact: Family groups laugh together at dawn and dusk to stake out their territory.
birds.nursery: Laughs loudly at nothing in particular, usually at dawn.

birds.name: Indian Peafowl
birds.call: A loud, cat-like “may-AWWW” scream.
birds.fact: Only the males (peacocks) carry the famous train; the females are peahens.
birds.nursery: Screams to show off. Display intensifies in front of grandparents.

birds.name: Blue-footed Booby
birds.call: Males give thin whistles; females honk and grunt.
birds.fact: Males strut to show off their feet — the bluer the feet, the healthier the bird.
birds.nursery: Also obsessed with own feet. Will put them in mouth for closer inspection.

birds.name: Canada Goose
birds.call: Loud, resonant “ha-ronk” honks.
birds.fact: Pairs usually mate for life and families migrate together.
birds.nursery: Honks to announce arrivals, departures and empty bottles.

birds.name: Mallard
birds.call: The classic descending “QUACK-quack-quack” (females); males give a quiet rasp.
birds.fact: Only female mallards make the loud, classic quack.
birds.nursery: Bath-time specialist. Can be lured with a rubber decoy.

birds.name: Red-tailed Hawk
birds.call: A hoarse, screaming “keee-eeee-arr” — the “eagle” sound from movies.
birds.fact: Films routinely dub this hawk’s scream over Bald Eagles, whose real call is much less dramatic.
birds.nursery: Piercing scream used to locate parents anywhere in the house.

photo.artist: Becky Matsubara from El Sobrante, California

birds.name: Bald Eagle
birds.call: Surprisingly weak, high, giggling chirps and whistles.
birds.fact: Its real voice is so un-majestic that movies swap in a Red-tailed Hawk.
birds.nursery: Majestic appearance, giggly little voice. Very relatable.

photo.artist: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK

birds.name: Blue Jay
birds.call: Loud “jeer! jeer!” calls, plus whistles, squeaks and gurgles.
birds.fact: Blue Jays can imitate Red-tailed Hawk screams remarkably well.
birds.nursery: Loud, opinionated, and an excellent mimic of the household.

birds.name: Black-capped Chickadee
birds.call: “Chick-a-dee-dee-dee” and a sweet, whistled “fee-bee”.
birds.fact: More “dee” notes in the call signals a more dangerous predator nearby.
birds.nursery: Extra “dees” indicate a high-threat situation, such as a nail trim.

photo.artist: No machine-readable author provided. Mdf assumed (based on copyright claims).

birds.name: Northern Cardinal
birds.call: Clear, slurred whistles: “cheer-cheer-cheer” or “birdie-birdie-birdie”.
birds.fact: Female cardinals sing too, sometimes from the nest to tell the male to bring food.
birds.nursery: Sings from the nest (crib) to request room service.

birds.name: American Robin
birds.call: Cheery caroling: “cheerily, cheer-up, cheerio”.
birds.fact: Robins find worms mostly by sight, cocking their heads to look.
birds.nursery: First to wake. Caroling begins before dawn whether you’re ready or not.

birds.name: Sandhill Crane
birds.call: A rolling, bugling rattle that carries for miles.
birds.fact: A long, coiled windpipe gives their call its trumpet-like resonance.
birds.nursery: Rattling bugle call, typically deployed in the car seat.

birds.name: Great Blue Heron
birds.call: Deep, harsh croaks: “frahnk”.
birds.fact: Herons stand motionless for long stretches, then strike in a flash.
birds.nursery: Long motionless stares followed by sudden lunges at the dog.

birds.name: Emu
birds.call: Deep drumming and booming, resonated in an inflatable throat pouch.
birds.fact: Female emus make the booming drum calls; males mostly grunt.
birds.nursery: Low rumbling noises, occasionally from the diaper region.

birds.name: Atlantic Puffin
birds.call: A low, growling purr, like a tiny chainsaw.
birds.fact: Puffins can carry a dozen or more small fish crosswise in their bills.
birds.nursery: Growls contentedly. Tries to fit as much as possible in mouth at once.

birds.name: African Penguin
birds.call: A loud, donkey-like bray.
birds.fact: It used to be called the “jackass penguin” because of that bray.
birds.nursery: Brays when food is late by even one minute.

recordings.recordist: Jorge de Leon Cardozo & Susan Hochgraf

birds.name: Red Junglefowl (Rooster)
birds.call: “Cock-a-doodle-doo!” plus clucks, cackles and alarm calls.
birds.fact: Roosters crow on an internal body clock, not just in response to sunrise.
birds.nursery: Crows at sunrise. Also at 4:45 a.m. Also at nap time.

birds.name: Laughing Gull
birds.call: A raucous “ha-ha-ha-haaah” laugh.
birds.fact: Laughing Gulls are notorious snack thieves on Atlantic beaches.
birds.nursery: Laughs at you, then steals your snack.

birds.name: Herring Gull
birds.call: Loud, ringing “kyow-kyow-kyow” long calls and yelps.
birds.fact: Chicks peck the red spot on a parent’s bill to ask for food.
birds.nursery: Pecks parent’s face to request food. Basically the same thing.

birds.name: Sulphur-crested Cockatoo
birds.call: An ear-splitting, raucous screech.
birds.fact: Sydney cockatoos learned to open wheelie bins, and taught each other how.
birds.nursery: Ear-splitting screech. Will learn to open cupboards soon.

birds.name: Tawny Frogmouth
birds.call: A low, steady “oom-oom-oom-oom”.
birds.fact: When threatened it freezes and pretends to be a broken branch.
birds.nursery: Low drowsy humming. Pretends to be asleep when you check on them.

birds.name: Common Potoo
birds.call: A haunting, descending series of mournful whistles.
birds.fact: Potoos have notches in their eyelids so they can watch while their eyes look closed.
birds.nursery: Mournful wail at bedtime. Eyes not fully closed. Watching.

birds.name: Northern Bobwhite
birds.call: A clear, rising whistle: “bob-WHITE!”
birds.fact: Coveys roost in a tight circle, tails in and heads out, to watch for predators.
birds.nursery: Whistles own name. Requires a ring of stuffed animals to sleep.

photo.artist: Matt Tillett from Cumberland, MD, USA

birds.name: Eurasian Bittern
birds.call: A deep “BOOM” like blowing across a bottle, audible for miles.
birds.fact: For its size it is one of the loudest birds in Europe.
birds.nursery: Booming sounds of unclear origin. Investigate diaper.

birds.name: Common Cuckoo
birds.call: The classic “cuck-oo”.
birds.fact: Cuckoos lay their eggs in other birds’ nests and let them raise the chick.
birds.nursery: Successfully gets grandparents to raise them for an afternoon.

photo.artist: Andy Morffew from Itchen Abbas, Hampshire, UK

birds.name: Killdeer
birds.call: A shrill, repeated “kill-deer, kill-deer”.
birds.fact: Killdeer fake a broken wing to lure predators away from the nest.
birds.nursery: Fakes dramatic injury to get out of tummy time.

birds.name: Northern Mockingbird
birds.call: An endless medley of borrowed songs, each phrase repeated 2–6 times.
birds.fact: Males can learn 200+ songs, including car alarms and squeaky gates.
birds.nursery: Repeats everything you say, at the worst possible moment.

birds.name: Kea
birds.call: A loud, descending “keee-aaa”, plus a warble that gets other kea playing.
birds.fact: The world’s only alpine parrot, famous for dismantling parked cars.
birds.nursery: Will disassemble anything within reach. Childproofing recommended.

birds.name: Common Eider
birds.call: Males coo a soft, surprised “ah-OOO”; females growl.
birds.fact: Eiders line their nests with the ultra-soft down that gives us eiderdown.
birds.nursery: Soft “ah-OOO” of mild surprise at own hands.
